content.title: Beast mode: Jonathan Young of Gulf Shores shines in latest ‘Survivor’ episode
content.text: Alabama Life & CultureThe third episode of the 42nd season of "Survivor" featured an immunity challenge tailor-made for the skills of Jonathan Young of Orange Beach. Young, fourth from left, prepares to dive into a rough surf that has some of his fellow competitors looking unsteady. Photo: Robert Voets/CBS Entertainment ©2022 CBS Broadcasting, Inc. All Rights Reserved.CBS/Robert VoetsBy Lawrence Specker | lspecker@al.com“This is an amazing performance to watch,” said “Survivor” mastermind Jeff Probst during the show’s newest episode, and he was talking about Jonathan Young of Gulf Shores.It was pretty amazing. In the first two episodes of the season, Young’s Taku tribe took a beating, losing one member to medical concerns and being forced to vote out another. But the third episode of the show’s 42nd season brought an immunity challenge tailor-made to showcase the man from Lower Alabama.Young has worked on in beach services for years. His pursuits include spearfishing and he’s a fitness buff who conspicuously outclasses the rest of the castaways in physical prowess. A representative of Guinness World Records confirmed to AL.com that Young previously held the record for most chin-ups in a minute while wearing a 100-pound pack, with 15. (Since then it has been bumped up to 19.)Related:Meet Alabama’s Jonathan Young, who’s hitting the beach on ‘Survivor’‘Survivor:’ How did Alabama’s Jonathan Young fare in the premiere?‘Survivor:’ Alabama’s Jonathan Young and his tribe suffer another lossEpisode three’s challenge involved swimming, diving and carrying a heavy ladder, all in a rough surf that probably would have had at least one red flag flying on the beaches Young calls home. Young went into beast mode. He didn’t just singlehandedly carry the ladder where it needed to go, he went back to help teammates who couldn’t keep up. Then, standing in water up to his neck, he raised the ladder up and held it firm while another teammate climbed it. It was like a Captain America beefcake shot from an Avengers movie. “I’ve rarely seen an individual performance like that,” said Probst.Jonathan Young of Gulf Shores gives "Survivor" teammate Maryanne Oketch a little help during an immunity challenge. Photo: Robert Voets/CBS Entertainment ©2022 CBS Broadcasting, Inc. All Rights Reserved.CBS/Robert VoetsJust how commanding was Young’s performance? He carried that ladder solo for the Taku tribe. The Vati and Ika tribes, each with four people trying to work together, flailed so badly at the same task that Probst finally called it off. Essentially, he pronounced the game a draw and let Ika and Vati have a shootout for second place. “We’ve never done this in the history of survivor,” he said.Ika won it, barely, securing immunity. Vati, which has seemed to have a high potential for drama, lived up to expectations.This season of “Survivor,” like the one before it, is running on a faster timetable and uses some immunity gimmicks that force players into risky decisions. Among other possibilities, players can gain or lose votes. That all came into play in Vati’s tribal council: The usual scuffle to secure alliances was complicated by the fact that retired firefighter Mike Turner and recruiter Chanelle Howell both had lost their votes.Had that not been the case, actor Lydia Meredith might have gone home on the first ballot. Instead there was a tie between her and designer Jenny Kim. The second vote was another tie. Then it came down to a discussion -- and if the discussion had failed, it was going to come down to a drawing.It was like watching one of those SEC grudge matches with so many overtimes that you wonder if the coaches will have to come out and resolve it by rock-paper-scissors.But analytics director Hai Giang stood rock-solid in his support for Lydia. Law clerk and budding villain Daniel Strunk lined up with him to vote out Jenny. Daniel also loudly blamed Chanelle for his actions, to her outrage.That leaves Vati with a messy 3-2 split, with Mike and Chanelle on the short end. Making it worse, Mike has no vote and a partial immunity idol that seems to be more of a liability than an asset.As for Taku, they won a toolkit and some fruit, which they were quick to trade for fishing gear. They’re still the smallest tribe, but their position no longer looks as desperate as it did a week ago.I've worked as a Mobile-based reporter for the Press-Register and AL.com for more than 25 years.
